problem:
Consider the following partitions:

- ${P}_{1}={{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}}$ is a partition of the interval $[0,1]$

- ${P}_{2}={{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}}$ is a partition of the interval $[1,2]$

Calculate ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}3Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j},$ where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1}.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following partitions:

- ${P}_{1}={{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}}$ is a partition of the interval $[2,4]$

- ${P}_{2}={{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}}$ is a partition of the interval $[3,7]$

Calculate ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}5Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j},$ where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple and product rules, we can write the summation as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}5Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} & =5{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} \\  & =5{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}$ and ${\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}$ are just the lengths of the intervals $[2,4]$ and $[3,7]$ respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i} & =4-2=2, \\ {\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j} & =7-3=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining our results, we have

$$
5{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}=5\cdot 2\cdot 4=40.
$$
